citation: Department of Microbiology, Government Medical College Srinagar. Antibiogram, January 2024 to June 2024. Srinagar: Government Medical College; 2024.
reporting: Percent susceptible. Overall Gram-negative and Gram-positive tables (all specimens and locations) with the number of isolates and a split by location (inpatients, OPD, ICU); blood and urine tables by location (IPD, OPD, ICU) with n per location; ICU tracheal aspirate tables (Gram-negative and S. aureus) with n.
method: CLSI M100, 34th edition (2024). The report states that organisms with fewer than 30 isolates were excluded (applied to the overall tables); vancomycin for S. aureus was not tested (no MIC method available).

verification.note: All tables parsed from the PDF text layer (words rebuilt from character positions, because the scaled glyphs defeat pdfplumber word extraction, and assigned to columns by the table ruling lines or header positions); every value, n and location label then compared by eye with the rendered pages (scale 2.5 whole pages; pages 2, 4 and 6 again at scale 3.2 in two halves each), 2026-09-26.

notes: Half-yearly antibiogram (January to June 2024) of the Department of Microbiology, GMC Srinagar. IPD (inpatient wards) is recorded as ward; ICU is separate. The overall tables are recorded as all specimens, all settings; the ICU tracheal aspirate tables as respiratory, ICU. The overall Gram-negative table prints genus-level rows (Acinetobacter sp. n=30, Klebsiella sp. n=56, Pseudomonas sp. n=44) beside the species rows, and the blood table a Pseudomonas spp. row beside P. aeruginosa; the app has one key per genus, so only the species rows are recorded (see excluded). Many location and tracheal aspirate cells print a value where the overall table prints "-" (not tested) for the same organism and drug (e.g. E. coli ampicillin-sulbactam, Klebsiella tobramycin); these are marked as conflicts. Counts: the inpatients, OPD and ICU columns of the overall tables are recorded as all specimens by location (species rows only); for every organism they sum to fewer than the table's printed number of isolates (e.g. E. coli 548 of 575), and their ICU figures are smaller than the ICU isolates of the tracheal aspirate table alone for A. baumannii (42 against 52, or 76 with the 24 blood ICU isolates), K. pneumoniae (13 against 41) and E. coli (17 against 18), and smaller than the blood, urine and tracheal aspirate ICU rows together for P. aeruginosa (35 against 20, 1 and 26) and S. aureus (9 against 7 and 6); B. cepacia has 25 ICU isolates in the overall table but 28 in the blood ICU row. So the location columns do not agree with the specimen tables. Zero-isolate strata of the blood and urine tables are recorded as 0 counts. Many blood, urine and tracheal aspirate strata have fewer than 30 isolates, and several printed percentages are not possible for the printed n (marked with a caution). Vancomycin was not tested for S. aureus. P. aeruginosa overall cefepime (100%) contradicts the blood and urine tables and is marked as a conflict.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 386 cells (seeded sample 96), all 46 row n, organisms and settings, and all 34 counts re-read against the page images (whole pages at scale 2.5, table crops at scale 3 to 4) before comparing with the file; 0 transcription errors and no IPD/OPD/ICU swaps (page 7 prints vancomycin before linezolid, page 5 after it; both mapped correctly; the blood IPD K. pneumoniae and tracheal aspirate K. pneumoniae ceftazidime cells are blank on the page and correctly left out).

The 19 conflicts are confirmed as printed: 18 cells where the overall table (page 2) prints "-" (not tested) but a location or tracheal aspirate table prints a value (E. coli ampicillin-sulbactam 0 in blood IPD and ICU, urine IPD and ICU and tracheal aspirates; K. pneumoniae ampicillin-sulbactam 0 in blood IPD, urine IPD and ICU and tracheal aspirates, and tobramycin 18.8, 33.3 and 33.3 in urine IPD, OPD and ICU; A. baumannii ceftriaxone 0 in blood IPD and ICU and tracheal aspirates, and Acinetobacter spp. urine IPD; E. coli urine IPD aztreonam 100 and tobramycin 66.7), and overall P. aeruginosa cefepime 100 against 24% and 30% (blood IPD and ICU) and 71.4% (urine OPD). The only other such cell, urine IPD K. pneumoniae ampicillin 0 (overall IR), is already marked intrinsic.

Cautions for percentages no whole number of isolates gives are confirmed as printed: blood ICU A. baumannii imipenem 24.3 (n=24), urine ICU K. pneumoniae piperacillin-tazobactam 50 (n=1), tracheal aspirate E. coli (5 figures, n=18) and P. aeruginosa (3 figures, n=26); blood ICU E. coli imipenem 50 and meropenem 100 (n=4) are as printed.

ICU counts: the row and file notes are correct that the overall table's ICU column is smaller than the tracheal aspirate ICU isolates for A. baumannii (42 against 52), K. pneumoniae (13 against 41) and E. coli (17 against 18), but only the A. baumannii tracheal aspirate row had a note. The ICU column is also smaller than the blood, urine and tracheal aspirate ICU rows together for P. aeruginosa (35 against 47) and S. aureus (9 against 13), and than the blood ICU row alone for B. cepacia (25 against 28). Added these to notes and a note to each of those rows. The overall table's location columns sum to less than its printed n for every organism, as the row notes say.

Against the full-year 2024 report (GMC_SRINAGAR_2024): several full-year figures are impossible if this report's isolates are part of the full-year strata (e.g. blood Burkholderia, urine ICU E. coli carbapenems, blood ICU Pseudomonas); these are marked in that file. Blood OPD A. baumannii has 2 isolates here but the full-year blood table has none.
Lead 2026-09-26: the full-year 2024 report contradicts some of these figures (listed as conflicts in GMC_SRINAGAR_2024); these half-year figures are kept as printed.
